title: Kingdom of Bahrain
capsule: Following independence from Britain on 15 August 1971, Bahrain operated as the 'State of Bahrain' under Emir Isa bin Salman Al Khalifa, joining the United Nations and Arab League and developing an oil- and finance-based economy centered on Manama. A 2001 referendum on the National Action Charter led the country's ruler, Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, to proclaim the constitutional monarchy the 'Kingdom of Bahrain' on 14 February 2002, upgrading his own title from emir to king and introducing an elected lower house alongside an appointed upper chamber. The kingdom weathered a major political crisis during the 2011 Arab Spring protests, suppressed with Gulf Cooperation Council military assistance, and remains ruled by the Al Khalifa dynasty into the 2020s.
